from collections.abc import Iterator
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

from app.utils import routes


def test_components_and_charts_preserve_generated_order(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    generated_routes = {
        "getting_started": [],
        "utilities": [],
        "resources": [],
        "components": [
            {"title": "Typography", "order": 0},
            {"title": "Accordion", "order": 1},
        ],
        "charts": [
            {"title": "Zebra Chart", "order": 0},
            {"title": "Area Chart", "order": 1},
        ],
    }
    def fake_generate_doc_routes(
        section: str,
        _base_path: str,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        return generated_routes[section]

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        routes,
        "generate_doc_routes",
        fake_generate_doc_routes,
    )

    result = routes.build_all_routes()

    assert result["components"] == generated_routes["components"]
    assert result["charts"] == generated_routes["charts"]


def test_resources_and_utilities_remain_sorted_by_title(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    generated_routes = {
        "getting_started": [],
        "utilities": [
            {"title": "Zebra Utility", "order": 0},
            {"title": "Alpha Utility", "order": 1},
        ],
        "resources": [
            {"title": "Zebra Resource", "order": 0},
            {"title": "Alpha Resource", "order": 1},
        ],
        "components": [],
        "charts": [],
    }
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        routes,
        "generate_doc_routes",
        lambda section, _base_path: generated_routes[section],
    )

    result = routes.build_all_routes()

    assert [item["title"] for item in result["utilities"]] == [
        "Alpha Utility",
        "Zebra Utility",
    ]
    assert [item["title"] for item in result["resources"]] == [
        "Alpha Resource",
        "Zebra Resource",
    ]


def test_generate_doc_routes_sorts_by_frontmatter_order_and_url_ties(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    docs_path = tmp_path / "components"
    docs_path.mkdir()
    markdown = {
        "zulu.md": '---\ntitle: "Zulu"\ndescription: "Tie entry"\norder: 1\n---\n',
        "late.md": '---\ntitle: "Late"\ndescription: "Later entry"\norder: 2\n---\n',
        "default.md": '---\ntitle: "Default"\ndescription: "Default order"\n---\n',
        "alpha.md": '---\ntitle: "Alpha"\ndescription: "Tie entry"\norder: 1\n---\n',
        "aardvark.md": '---\ntitle: "Aardvark"\ndescription: "Default-order tie"\norder: 0\n---\n',
    }
    paths = []
    for filename, content in markdown.items():
        path = docs_path / filename
        path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
        paths.append(path)

    # Reverse both tied URL groups to prove tie ordering ignores glob order.
    glob_order = [paths[2], paths[4], paths[0], paths[3], paths[1]]

    def fake_glob(_self: Path, _pattern: str) -> Iterator[Path]:
        return iter(glob_order)

    monkeypatch.setattr(routes.constants, "DOCS_BASE_DIR", tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.setattr(routes.Path, "glob", fake_glob)

    generated = routes.generate_doc_routes("components", "docs/components/")

    assert [item["title"] for item in generated] == [
        "Aardvark",
        "Default",
        "Alpha",
        "Zulu",
        "Late",
    ]

import reflex as rx

from components.charts.chart_tooltip import chart_tooltip, chart_tooltip_content

data = [
    {"month": "Jan", "desktop": 186, "mobile": 80},
    {"month": "Feb", "desktop": 305, "mobile": 200},
    {"month": "Mar", "desktop": 237, "mobile": 120},
    {"month": "Apr", "desktop": 73, "mobile": 190},
    {"month": "May", "desktop": 209, "mobile": 130},
    {"month": "Jun", "desktop": 214, "mobile": 140},
]


def _legend_item(device: str, index: int) -> rx.Component:
    return rx.el.div(
        rx.el.div(class_name=f"h-3 w-3 rounded-sm bg-chart-{index + 1}"),
        rx.el.p(device, class_name="text-xs text-foreground"),
        class_name="flex flex-row items-center gap-x-2",
    )


def chart_example_with_custom_legends() -> rx.Component:

    return rx.el.div(
        rx.recharts.bar_chart(
            rx.recharts.cartesian_grid(
                horizontal=True,
                vertical=False,
                class_name="opacity-30",
            ),
            rx.recharts.bar(
                data_key="desktop",
                fill="var(--chart-1)",
                radius=4,
                is_animation_active=False,
            ),
            rx.recharts.bar(
                data_key="mobile",
                fill="var(--chart-2)",
                radius=4,
                is_animation_active=False,
            ),
            rx.recharts.x_axis(
                data_key="month",
                axis_line=False,
                tick_size=10,
                tick_line=False,
                custom_attrs={"fontSize": "12px"},
                interval="preserveStartEnd",
            ),
            chart_tooltip(),
            data=data,
            width="100%",
            height=250,
            class_name=chart_tooltip_content(
                [1, 2],
                "square",
                series_names=["desktop", "mobile"],
            ),
        ),
        rx.el.div(
            rx.foreach(
                ["Desktop", "Mobile"],
                _legend_item,
            ),
            class_name="flex items-center gap-4 justify-center",
        ),
        class_name="w-full",
    )

Pie Charts are ideal for showing changes over time or the magnitude of multiple datasets stacked together. They combine the smoothness of line charts with the visual impact of filled areas.

## Examples

>**Note**: The chart example charts below are wrapped in [Card](/docs/components/card). Make sure to have the component installed before using any of the examples.

Displays labels that appear dynamically when hovering over chart segments.

Shows labels positioned inside each pie segment for compact presentation.
--DEMO(piechart_v3)--

## Legend
Adds a built-in legend for easy segment identification and reference.
--DEMO(piechart_v4)--

## Doughnut
Renders the pie chart with a hollow center for a modern doughnut style.
--DEMO(piechart_v5)--

# --- PATHS ---
DOCS_SOURCE_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "docs"
MARKDOWN_OUTPUT_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "assets" / "docs"
DYNAMIC_LOAD_DIRS = ["app/www/library", "components/ui"]

# Maps lowercased names to (object, name as defined) for every loaded callable or component namespace instance.
Registry = dict[str, tuple[Any, str]]


def dynamic_load_components(dirs: list[str]) -> Registry:

    """Names passed as a plain identifier (not a lambda) for the ``render_fn``
    (second positional argument) of an ``rx.foreach(iterable, render_fn)`` call.

    names: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):

            and node.func.attr == "foreach"
            and len(node.args) >= 2
            and isinstance(node.args[1], ast.Name)
